terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: Before continuing, please read and accept the MVP Tracker terms of use.

purpose.title: 1. Purpose
purpose.text: MVP Tracker is a personal Valorant stats-tracking app. It is intended for private, non-commercial use, only to view the statistics of your own account.

account.title: 2. Your account and API key
account.text: You confirm that the linked Riot account is yours. You are responsible for your personal HenrikDev API key and how it is used. The app never accesses the Riot client or any game files or processes.

data.title: 3. Data
data.text: Your matches and settings are stored locally on your computer. Your MVP Tracker account (email, profile, social features) is hosted by Supabase. Anonymous usage and error data may be collected to improve the app. You can request deletion of your account by contacting us from within the app.

community.title: 4. Community features
community.text: Messages, leaderboards, announcements and tournaments must remain respectful. Any hateful, illegal or fraudulent content (cheating on leaderboards, impersonation...) may lead to account suspension.

liability.title: 5. Liability
liability.text: The app is provided "as is", with no guarantee of availability or accuracy of the data, which comes from third-party services. We cannot be held liable for an outage of those services or for any decision made from the statistics shown.

changes.title: 6. Changes
changes.text: These terms may change along with the app. If the change is significant, your agreement will be requested again.

terms.riotNotice: MVP Tracker isn't endorsed by Riot Games and doesn't reflect the views or opinions of Riot Games or anyone officially involved in producing or managing Riot Games properties. Riot Games, and all associated properties are trademarks or registered trademarks of Riot Games, Inc.

aimTrainer.title: Aim Trainer
aimTrainer.hint: A 3D aim trainer calibrated to your real Valorant sensitivity: 20+ modes, a daily challenge, leaderboards and a Sensitivity Finder to find your sensitivity.

modes.flickDesc: One target at a time, hit it as fast as you can. The basics.
modes.gridshotDesc: Several targets at once: chain them with no downtime.
modes.trackingBeginnerDesc: The target moves continuously, slowly and predictably — keep your crosshair on it.
modes.trackingIntermediateDesc: The target moves faster and changes direction more often.
modes.trackingDesc: The target moves fast and erratically — the toughest tier.
modes.reflexDesc: Targets vanish fast: miss one and it counts against you.
modes.microDesc: Tiny, closely spaced targets for fine precision.
modes.orbitDesc: Targets circle around: anticipation and tracking.
modes.peekDesc: A target peeks out from behind cover, left or right, at Valorant's real strafe speed. Only the head counts.
modes.trackingMultiDesc: Two moving targets at once, crosshair held on whichever one you choose to follow.
modes.strafeDesc: The target crosses the screen in a straight line at constant speed, like a real strafe — trains recoil control while on the move.
modes.patrolSlowDesc: A target walking slowly left to right, no shooting — keep your crosshair on it.
modes.patrolDesc: A target walking left to right, no shooting — keep your crosshair on it as long as possible to score.
modes.patrolFastDesc: A target running left to right, no shooting — the most demanding constant-speed tier.
modes.patrolMultiDesc: Speed (and sometimes direction) changes mid-session — no fixed rhythm to anticipate.
modes.switchModeDesc: Several numbered targets: hit them in the order shown. Hitting one out of order counts as a miss, even if you land the shot.
modes.strafeTapDesc: The target drifts and takes several hits before it actually resets — simulates a mid-range spray on a moving target.
modes.precisionDesc: A tiny target, barely visible for as long as it's shown. The hardest combo: aim fine AND fast.
modes.popcornDesc: Several targets pop up and vanish fast, all over the screen — pure reaction under pressure.
modes.snapHoldDesc: A flick isn't enough: you need to stay settled on the target for a short beat for the shot to count — stops lucky flicks that land by accident.
modes.flashDodgeDesc: Classic target shooting, but a flash (Skye or Phoenix, at random) comes from an unpredictable direction — turn away in time to dodge it, or the screen goes white.
modes.sprayDesc: Hold the click on a fixed target and steer the mouse to counter the recoil and stay on it, like real spray training.
modes.headshotDuelDesc: Agents with Valorant's size and movement speed strafe around the Monastery A site. Only a headshot kills them (160 damage).
modes.ascentDuelDesc: The new Belvedere map, a Venetian-style A site: flowered facades, Heaven, Hell, the big door and the floating city. Only headshots count.
modes.sniperQuickscopeDesc: An enemy appears in the open for barely a second: scope and shoot in one motion. A body shot is enough.
modes.sniperNoscopeDesc: Caught too close to scope: scope disabled, the enemy moves at 12-16 m. The Operator survival reflex.
modes.sniperAngleHoldDesc: Keep your crosshair on the marked angle: the enemy swings out without warning and ducks back fast. Pre-aim discipline.
modes.sniperRepeekDesc: After every kill, the next one comes out of a different angle. Don’t stay scoped on a dead angle.
modes.sniperBoltDesc: Three enemies in the open, a bolt to cycle between every shot: every missed bullet is costly.
modes.sniperScopeSpeedDesc: The enemy is already there, far away. Your scope drops at every spawn: get on target and shoot as fast as you can.

skinDesc.symbiote: A breathing chitin exoskeleton: membrane ribcage, pressurised fluid, three blinking eyes, muzzle valves; it contracts on every shot.
skinDesc.heliopause: White ceramic and brushed gold: containment coils, a plasma tube, a gyroscopic reactor, electric arcs; cascading magnetic compression on fire.
skinDesc.reliquary: A cursed relic in forged iron and tarnished gold: a shrine, arches burning with spectral flame, skulls with glowing eyes, a censer, smoke.
skinDesc.nullbyte: A hacked weapon: smoked-glass handguard over a circuit board, RGB glitches, holographic console, ammo and latency, a square flash.
skinDesc.patchbay: A modular synth in brushed aluminium and walnut: modules that recoil in cascade, a live oscilloscope, swinging patch cables, a keyboard magazine and a speaker muzzle. Every shot plays a note.
skinDesc.downforce: A race car in woven carbon and fluo yellow: inverted-wing handguard, DRS flaps that open on each shot, sidepods, a rear wing and twin blued-titanium exhausts spitting blue flames.
skinDesc.singularity: A weapon carved from the void: a black hole held by golden gimbals floats by its side, its accretion disk spinning and swallowing debris. A mini singularity at the muzzle, gravitational waves on each shot. It spirals out of the black hole.
skinDesc.metamorph: A mecha pistol: ceramic armor, flaps opening on induction coils, electric rails, a turbine, a reactor iris and an energy cell. It unfolds from a cube.
skinDesc.rift: An obsidian shell cracked open on another dimension, levitating shards, a portal muzzle and a vortex scope. Every shot tears reality. It emerges from a rift opening in mid-air.
skinDesc.origami: Folded from washi and vermilion paper: gliding cranes, paper lanterns, breathing pleats, a lotus muzzle. Cranes take flight with every shot. It unfolds sheet by sheet.
skinDesc.hive: A living hive: wax cells, glowing dripping honey, raised combs and a swarm of bees circling the weapon, panicking on each shot. The wax builds it cell by cell.
skinDesc.voxel: A retro game weapon: blinking pixel art, a cube heart and bolt, a lives and ammo HUD, cube explosions and “+100”. It drops from the sky bouncing, then “READY!”.
skinDesc.maelstrom: Water held in shape: koi swimming inside, bubbles, caustics, a rippling surface, a whirlpool around the barrel. It rises from a vortex.
skinDesc.sumi: Ink painting: mountain washes, a red sun, flowing ink ribbons, a calligraphy brush muzzle, an ensō on each shot. A giant brush paints it.
skinDesc.arcade: A pocket arcade cabinet: a real mini game runs on the screens, chasing bulbs, a joystick, a coin slot. A coin drops in and the screen powers on like an old TV.
skinDesc.hanabi: A summer night: lacquer painted with twinkling fireworks, sparklers, rockets fired with every shot that burst in the sky, a red lantern. It is born from a firework.
skinDesc.mirage: Desert sandstone with ochre strata, gold inlays and turquoise: the wind blows sand off it, an hourglass flows and flips, a stone ring turns. It rises from a dune.
skinDesc.candy: The candy shop: dripping icing, sprinkles, candy cane, chocolate, a donut muzzle, gummy bears, lollipops, orbiting sweets. Each part pops in like jelly.
skinDesc.kintsugi: Blue and white porcelain, broken and mended with gold: gold flows through the cracks, shards float around. It pieces itself together, then gold fills the cracks.
skinDesc.locomotive: A steam engine: spoked wheels, turning rods and pistons, a smoking stack, a cowcatcher, a headlamp, a brass scope. It pulls into the station on its rails.
skinDesc.kaleidoscope: A mirror with a turning kaleidoscope, a scope of colored glass, prisms scattering light, a mandala muzzle. It closes like a rosette.
skinDesc.marble: Gold-veined Carrara marble, a Greek key frieze, a laurel wreath, Ionic volutes, golden leaves on each shot. It is carved out of a crumbling block.
skinDesc.weaver: Indigo silk embroidered with gold: golden strings vibrating like a harp, a spool, a running shuttle. Every shot plucks the strings. Threads from a spindle weave it.
skinDesc.corsair: Ship wood, brass, a leather-wrapped spyglass, ropes, a compass, a flapping black flag, a cannon muzzle, a rain of doubloons. It bursts out of a treasure chest.
skinDesc.lithosphere: Magnetic geode: levitating basalt blocks bound by force lines, prismatic crystals, an open geode and a quartz tip; on each shot the rock splits apart and snaps back in a cascade.
skinDesc.titan: Mech armour: thick plates, a finned shroud, pistons that compress on each shot, a gyroscopic reactor in the stock.
skinDesc.arcane: Grimoire leather and golden runes, three rotating magic circles, a focus gem, orbiting pages and mana streams.
skinDesc.mercury: Living liquid metal: the surface truly ripples, floating and falling drops, a crown of spikes, chrome splashes.
skinDesc.sylvan: Enchanted forest: bark and glowing sap, moss, vines, bioluminescent mushrooms, fireflies and spores.
skinDesc.spectre: Ghost samurai: indigo lacquer, a tsuba, armour plates, a spectral aura, blue flames and will-o-wisps.
skinDesc.orbital: Recon satellite: deployable solar panels, a dish, an orbital ring and blue-flame thrusters.
skinDesc.ossuary: Carved from dragon bones: a skull whose jaw snaps, a spine, ribs, spikes and embers.
skinDesc.stained: Cathedral window: backlit stained glass, gothic arches, a rose window with light rays, a bell that rings.
skinDesc.abyssal: Deep-sea anglerfish: glowing lure, photophores, waving fins, needle-toothed jaws.
skinDesc.supernova: A collapsing star: cracked crust over plasma, a molten star at the muzzle, solar flare arches.
skinDesc.chronos: Master of time: dials showing the real time, gears, a pendulum, time rings; time rewinds on every shot.
skinDesc.monarch: Monarch butterfly: wings beating on the slide, butterflies in flight, a swarm taking off on each shot.
skinDesc.scorpion: Desert predator: amber chitin, an articulated tail that strikes on each shot, pincers, sand.
skinDesc.quantum: Particle physics: an accelerator ring, orbiting electrons, a probability cloud, interference patterns.
skinDesc.harlequin: The king’s fool: red, black and gold diamonds, a ruff, jingling bells, orbiting cards, confetti.
skinDesc.aurora: Midnight-blue steel engraved with snowflakes where the northern lights dance; ribbons of light wave around the rifle.
skinDesc.sakura: Gold-lined black lacquer, sculpted cherry branches in bloom, falling petals and a paper lantern.
skinDesc.radiation: Rusted steel and hazard stripes, glowing radioactive vials, a gas mask filter and toxic fumes.
skinDesc.pharaoh: Gold and lapis lazuli, glyph friezes, a scarab that spreads its wings, a winged sun disk and a cobra at the muzzle.
skinDesc.hologram: The whole rifle as a projection: cyan light, scanlines, wireframe edges, glitches and orbiting data.
skinDesc.futuristic: Pearl-white ceramic and gunmetal, glowing cyan circuits and chevrons, ejected energy cells.
skinDesc.banana: The banana gun: it fires real bananas and ejects peels. Completely serious.
skinDesc.synthwave: Holographic black lacquer, retro grid and sunset, magenta and cyan neons, glitches and a chromatic flash.
skinDesc.kraken: Abyssal bronze, barnacles and bioluminescent glow, swaying coiled tentacles, bubbles and an ink cloud.
skinDesc.oni: Red lacquer and glowing gold kintsugi, bone horns, burning eyes, fangs, a swinging talisman, demonic aura.
skinDesc.prism: Cut from crystal: the mechanism shows through the glass, and light splits into a rainbow.
skinDesc.xeno: A living biomechanical weapon: acid veins beating like a heart, a spine, ribs, a toothed maw, dripping acid.
skinDesc.sniper: Bolt-action precision rifle: scope, bipod, fluted barrel and a full bolt cycle between shots.
skinDesc.glacier: Living ice with glinting facets, translucent crystals growing on the rifle, ice spikes at the muzzle, falling snow.
skinDesc.void: Black glass split by violet rifts, levitating shards, and a black hole at the muzzle swallowing matter.
skinDesc.phoenix: Crimson lacquer and golden feathers: wings of fire that spread on every shot, a golden beak and flickering flames.
skinDesc.storm: Lightning-veined armour, Tesla coils linked by live electric arcs, a railgun muzzle.
skinDesc.crown: Marble, royal blue enamel and baroque gold, precious stones, a crown on the scope and a shower of gold.
skinDesc.standard: The original Vandal: machined gunmetal steel, sand and black polymer, engravings and rivets.
skinDesc.magma: Cracked obsidian with flowing lava, basalt chunks, a smoking crater muzzle, lava drips and embers.
skinDesc.circuit: Ceramic and graphite, data-pulsing circuits, a glass magazine of energy cells, a holographic sight.
skinDesc.celeste: A fragment of the night sky: twinkling nebula, a solar system in the stock, a supernova on every shot.
skinDesc.jade: Light-veined jade wrapped by a golden dragon whose jaw opens to breathe emerald fire on every shot.
skinDesc.clockwork: Walnut, brass and copper: racing gears, a pressure gauge, pistons, an ether vial and steam.
skinDesc.glock: The sidearm, modelled to the millimetre: recoiling slide, ejected casing, smoke.
skinDesc.dune: Desert sand tones, from receiver to stock.
skinDesc.cobalt: Deep blue anodized receiver, charcoal parts.
skinDesc.tidal: Navy to turquoise fade, swept by a light reflection.
skinDesc.redline: All black, with a red magazine and accents pulsing to the rhythm of fire.
skinDesc.ivory: Silver slide, ivory frame and orange front dot.
skinDesc.sunset: Orange to magenta fade slide, swept by a golden reflection.
skinDesc.volt: Matte black, small parts pulsing electric green.
skinDesc.urban: Concrete grey and charcoal, clean and understated.
skinDesc.forest: Woodland greens, from stock to barrel.
skinDesc.amethyst: Deep purple fade, swept by a lilac reflection.
skinDesc.cryo: Frosted metal giving off an icy glow.

aimTrainer.howtoIntro: Real aim training, calibrated to your Valorant sensitivity. Nothing to install — it runs in a dedicated window.

aimTrainer.tutorialIntro: Two things to know before you start:
aimTrainer.tutorialSensText: Once the Aim Trainer is open, go to "Settings": enter the same DPI and sensitivity as your Valorant mouse settings, so aiming feels exactly the same as in-game. You can also pick your weapon and its skin there.
aimTrainer.tutorialLaunchText: Click "Open Aim Trainer" — a fullscreen window opens on its own menu. Pick a mode in "Training modes" (or "Headshot · Site A" to aim at moving agents) or click "Play" directly: your mouse gets captured, Esc to quit.
aimTrainer.customDesc: Set your own parameters — this mode isn't compared between players on any leaderboard.
aimTrainer.customIntro: The 20 standard modes are fixed so records stay comparable across everyone. Here, pick a starting mode then freely adjust every setting.
aimTrainer.presetsIntro: Your saved custom presets — load one directly, or create a new one.

aimTrainer.finderHint: Test several sensitivities to find yours
aimTrainer.finderIntro: Runs {{count}} back-to-back {{duration}}s tests around your current sensitivity, in random order (so warm-up and fatigue don't skew the comparison), then compares your hits and accuracy on each.
aimTrainer.finderResultsIntro: Score for each tested sensitivity: hits × accuracy. Hits count, and every miss is penalized — a sensitivity so low that you barely hit anything can't win.
aimTrainer.finderEdgeHintUp: The score is still rising at the high end of what you tested: the optimum is probably higher. Run another test centered on {{sens}} to refine it.
aimTrainer.finderEdgeHintDown: The score is still rising at the low end of what you tested: the optimum is probably lower. Run another test centered on {{sens}} to refine it.
aimTrainer.finderIndistinctHint: Your results are too close to pick a better sensitivity: keep yours, or run another test.
aimTrainer.finderSuggestedHint: Computed from the curve of your results — not necessarily one of the tested values, if the real optimum falls between two of them.

aimTrainer.themeFixedDesc: Pick an agent: they stay shown, with their color, every time you open it.

aim.name: Accuracy
aim.measures: Your share of shots to the head. It is the first lever to win your duels.
aim.how: Headshots ÷ total shots that hit, over all your analysed ranked matches. The score compares that percentage to 40%: 40% headshots = 100, 20% = 50. Your current percentage: {{value}}%.
aim.train: The Micro mode of the Aim Trainer makes you aim at tiny targets: it teaches you to aim fine instead of wide. 10 minutes before a match is enough.
tips: Keep your crosshair at head height on every angle, before you even see an enemy.
Settle your crosshair before shooting: one steady shot beats three sloppy body shots.
Take a step back in duels: you gain accuracy and your opponent has to come to you.
aim.goal: Go from {{current}}% to {{target}}% headshots over your next 20 ranked matches.

positioning.name: Positioning
positioning.measures: The share of your deaths that happen in the first 20 seconds of the round. The lower it is, the less you get caught off guard early.
positioning.how: We look at when in the round you die: the share of your deaths that happen in the first 20 seconds. Score = 100 − 2 × that share (0 at minimum): no early deaths = 100, 50% or more = 0. At least 10 deaths must be analysed ({{count}} here). Your current share: {{value}}%.
positioning.train: The Reflex mode trains you to react and neutralise an enemy who appears quickly, so you stop losing the opening duels.
tips: Do not peek first alone without information: wait for an ability or a teammate.
Take the angle later in the round: the first 20 seconds are the riskiest.
Use your smoke or flash before peeking instead of relying on your aim alone.
positioning.goal: Bring your early deaths from {{current}}% down to {{target}}% over your next 20 matches.

aggression.name: Aggression
aggression.measures: The share of rounds where you are in the very first duel (first kill or first death). Too low and you are always reacting.
aggression.how: Share of rounds where you are in the very first duel (first kill or first death): {{count}} rounds out of {{rounds}}. The score compares that share to 40%: one opening duel every 2.5 rounds = 100, an average player is around 20% = 50. Your opening duel win rate ({{percent}}%) does not count in the score.
aggression.train: The Peek mode trains you to step out and engage an appearing opponent quickly: exactly the motion of an opening duel.
tips: Call that you are entering, so your team follows and can trade you.
Pick the moment to take the first duel (right after an ability) instead of waiting.
Stay close to a teammate: an opening duel with a possible trade costs far less.
aggression.goal: Go from {{current}}% to {{target}}% of rounds where you take the first duel.

stability.name: Resilience
stability.measures: Your performance (K/D) in games played right after a loss, compared with your average. 70 = no drop.
stability.how: Your performance (K/D) in games played right after a loss (less than 100 minutes after the previous one started), compared with your average. 70 = no drop, 100 = you play better, 0 = sharp drop. Based on {{count}} games played after a loss (8 minimum).
stability.train: The Extreme Precision mode builds consistency under pressure: aiming fine AND fast, game after game.
tips: After a loss, take a 5-minute break before queueing again.
Switch agent or mode instead of replaying the same game on a loop.
Do a 5-minute aim warm-up before the next game.
stability.goal: Aim for a resilience score of {{target}} (currently {{current}}): no K/D drop after a loss.

versatility.name: Versatility
versatility.measures: The number of agents you truly master: at least 5 games each, with good results.
versatility.how: Agents you truly master: at least 5 games, with a 45% win rate or a K/D close to your average (at least 90% of it). The score rises more and more slowly and never reaches 100 (4 agents ≈ 70, 6 ≈ 82). Here {{count}} mastered out of {{total}} played.
versatility.train: Composition helps you find an agent that complements your main, to learn and then try in unranked.
tips: Pick a single new agent and play it for 5 unranked games.
Try an agent from a different role to understand what your teammates do.
Keep your main for important ranked games.

clutch.name: Clutch factor
clutch.measures: Your win rate when you are alone against several opponents.
clutch.how: Your win rate when you are in a clutch situation (alone against several opponents). The score is that win rate, computed from at least 3 situations: {{count}} situation(s) analysed.
clutch.train: The Snap-hold mode trains you to aim fast then hold your position: the reflex of a good clutch.
tips: Do not run at the enemies: isolate the duels one by one.
Use the time left: a clutch is often won against the clock, not by rushing.
Review your lost clutches to spot where you took the wrong duel.
clutch.goal: Go from {{current}}% to {{target}}% of clutches won.

duelistImpulsive.title: Impulsive duelist
duelistImpulsive.text: You're at the heart of round-opening duels, but it doesn't always pay off: you lose more than you win, or your performance drops after a loss. A real aggression engine, to be channelled.

clutchFragger.title: Clutch fragger
clutchFragger.text: You open rounds and close out tight situations: a rare combination of aggression and composure late in the round.

entryFragger.title: Entry fragger
entryFragger.text: You often take the first duel of the round and hold your own in it. A demanding role that opens space for your team from the start of the round.

aggressivePolyvalent.title: Versatile fragger
aggressivePolyvalent.text: You take the initiative AND master several different agents: a player who opens rounds without depending on a single kit.

clutchAllrounder.title: Complete all-rounder
clutchAllrounder.text: Several agents mastered, resilience after a loss, and solid clutch numbers: the most complete profile tracked here, with no glaring weakness.

quietFlexible.title: Quiet flexible
quietFlexible.text: You master several agents and bounce back well after a loss, but you're not the one looking for first contact. A profile that adapts to the team rather than the ego.

versatileTactician.title: Versatile tactician
versatileTactician.text: You master several agents and your performance holds after a loss. The flexible profile of a player who adapts to the team.

unstableCloser.title: Unstable but clutch
unstableCloser.text: Your performance drops after a loss, but when it really matters (one-versus-multiple), you show up more often than average. An interesting contrast to watch alongside the Tilt module.

inconsistentPlayer.title: Streaky player
inconsistentPlayer.text: Your performance tends to drop right after a loss. The Tilt module can help you spot the right moment to take a break.

clutchSpecialist.title: Clutch specialist
clutchSpecialist.text: You rely on a small core of mastered agents, but you're dangerous in clutch situations. Focused expertise that pays off exactly when it counts.

closer.title: Closer
closer.text: You might not dominate the start of rounds, but you're clutch: you convert an above-average number of one-versus-multiple situations.

quietSpecialist.title: Quiet specialist
quietSpecialist.text: Few agents mastered, little first initiative taken: a composed profile that would rather play its hand than force situations.

specialist.title: Specialist
specialist.text: You rely on a small core of agents rather than rotating. Focused expertise, at the cost of a bit of flexibility when a switch is needed.

steadyPillar.title: Steady pillar
steadyPillar.text: You don't look for first contact, but you bounce back very well after a loss. The kind of teammate the team can count on without thinking about it.

balancedPlayer.title: Balanced player
balancedPlayer.text: Nothing stands out strongly either way for now: a stable profile, with no excess or glaring weakness on the tracked axes.

weakness.title: Points to work on
weakness.none: Nothing to flag for now — your profile is balanced across every tracked axis.

aggression.title: Aggression
aggression.text: You win few first duels. The Aim Trainer's Peek mode trains exactly that: pushing out and engaging fast on a target that appears.

stability.title: Resilience
stability.text: Your performance often drops after a loss or a death streak. The Aim Trainer's Precision mode trains calm, controlled aim, useful for not tilting.

versatility.title: Versatility
versatility.text: You have few agents you perform on consistently. The Composition tool lets you explore other roles and prep a backup agent.

clutch.title: Clutch factor
clutch.text: You win few 1-vs-multiple situations. The Aim Trainer's Snap & Hold mode trains snapping onto a target then holding position, useful in clutches.

aim.title: Precision
aim.text: Your headshot percentage is low. The Aim Trainer's Micro mode forces you to hit tiny targets — exactly the aim it takes to land more headshots.

positioning.title: Positioning
positioning.text: You often die in the very first seconds of the round. The Aim Trainer's Reflex mode trains reacting and neutralizing fast as soon as an opponent appears.

welcome.tagline: Enter your Riot ID and API key to load your matches.
welcome.apiKeyHelp: The API key is used to fetch your matches from HenrikDev (the service the app uses to talk to Valorant) — it's free. Here's how:
welcome.apiKeyStep1: Click the button below — it opens the HenrikDev site in your browser.
welcome.apiKeyStep2: Sign in (with your Discord account if asked), then go to "API Keys" in the left menu.
welcome.apiKeyStep3: Click "Generate New Key" and pick the "Basic" type — that's the free one.
welcome.apiKeyStep4: Copy the long code that gets generated, come back here, and paste it into the "HenrikDev API key" field above.

accountGreeting.title: Hey {{name}}
accountGreeting.tagline: Your account is linked to this Valorant profile:
accountGreeting.aimText: Warm up your aim before launching Valorant — calibrated to your real sensitivity, 20 modes, daily challenge and progress tracking.

linkRiot.title: Link your Riot account
linkRiot.disclaimerWarning: Use your OWN Riot username here.
linkRiot.disclaimerMiddle: link this Valorant account to your MVP Tracker account — it's what will drive your goals, your Hall of Fame, your skin collection, etc. This is
linkRiot.disclaimerSuffix: just a preview: this Valorant account will be the one behind your tracker.
linkRiot.confirmYes: Yes, that's me — link this account
linkRiot.alreadyLinkedError: This Riot account is already linked to another MVP Tracker account — each Riot ID can only be linked to one account at a time.
linkRiot.genericLinkError: Linking failed. Try again in a moment.
linkRiot.noRecentGameError: This account exists, but HenrikDev (the service providing the stats) can't read its data: the problem is on their side, not your username. Try again in a few minutes, or after playing a new game.

account.suggestionPrefix_other: Based on your {{count}} tracked games, you mostly play
account.settingsHint: Signed in with your MVP Tracker account — your linked Riot ID stays independent from this account.
account.riotIdHint: If you changed your username IN-GAME, update it here so the tracker keeps finding your matches — this doesn't change the linked Valorant account, just the name it's looked up by.
account.riotIdMismatch: This Riot ID belongs to a different Valorant account — not yours. Check the spelling, or contact us if you think this is a mistake.
account.dailyOverlayHint: A small line in the top-right corner while Valorant runs: today's wins/losses, headshot % and K/D, via HenrikDev (never the client's local API). Resets each day.
account.dailyOverlaySettingsButton: Choose modes excluded from the score
account.dailyOverlayMovingHint: Turn on to drag the overlay anywhere on screen (outside a match), then turn off to lock its position. Always turned off automatically as soon as a match starts.
account.updateHint: Checks whether a new version of MVP Tracker is available.

updateStatus.available: Version {{version}} is available (you have {{current}}). It downloads in the background: the “Restart” button will appear at the top once it's ready. If nothing happens after a few minutes, download it directly.
updateStatus.ready: Version {{version}} is ready: click “Restart” at the top to install it.
updateStatus.dev: Not available in development mode: updates only apply to the installed app.
updateStatus.error: Couldn't check right now. Check your connection and try again.

account.autoLaunchLabel: Launch MVP Tracker at Windows startup
account.autoLaunchHint: The app launches in the background when your PC starts, minimized to the system tray (icon near the clock) — ping and tilt detection keep running without a window open.
account.tiltNotificationsHint: A Windows notification pops up when a losing streak or a performance dip is detected while you play. Turn off if you'd rather just check the Tilt tab yourself.
account.forgotPasswordSent: Email sent — check your inbox to reset your password.
account.forgotPasswordError: Failed to send — try again in a moment.
account.deleteReasonsHint: Tell us why (optional) — it helps us improve the app.

deleteReason.notWhatExpected: The app doesn't fit my needs
deleteReason.bugs: Too many bugs or technical issues
deleteReason.privacy: I'm concerned about my data's privacy

account.deleteAccountHint: Permanent and irreversible: your account, profile and all your data (clips, tournaments, messages...) will be deleted. No confirmation email will be sent.
account.deleteAccountError: Deletion failed — try again in a moment.
account.contactHint: An issue, a suggestion, a question? Write to us directly.
account.contactSent: Message sent — thanks, we'll get back to you as soon as possible.
account.contactError: Failed to send — try again in a moment.
account.perfLiteHint: Reduces animations and blur effects to make the app lighter on a modest PC. Turned on automatically on low-powered PCs; you can change it here.

heatmap.title: Heatmap
heatmap.description: Visualize where you die (or get kills) most often on each map, based on all your cached matches.

landing.subtitle: Pick your view: where you die and get kills, or where you win and lose your duels.

classic.desc: The heat map of your deaths and kills, map by map. Spot where you get hit the most.

duels.desc: Where you win and where you lose your duels, with the score and success rate per zone. On one game or on all of them.

duel.title: Duel heatmap
duel.description: Where you win and where you lose your duels. Each cell shows your won-lost duels; colour goes from red (you lose) to green (you win).
duel.noData: No duels on this map with these filters.
duel.hint: Click a coloured cell to see its duels: opponent, weapon, distance and round.
duel.noGames: No games played on a standard map yet.
duel.rankEmpty: Not enough duels yet (3 minimum per zone).
duel.fewDuels: Too few duels to show a trend.
duel.limits: Only duels decided by a kill are counted (Riot does not expose trades without a death). A duel is placed between you and your opponent.

analyse.clutchHint: A clutch is when you're the last teammate alive while at least one opponent is still alive.

dailyOverlaySettings.title: Session overlay
dailyOverlaySettings.intro: This small window shows up in the top-right corner while Valorant runs: your wins/losses, headshot % and K/D for the day, recalculated every 5 minutes.
dailyOverlaySettings.autoExcludeNote: Modes without a real win/loss (Deathmatch, Escalation, custom games...) are always excluded automatically. Check other modes here to exclude them too, e.g. Spike Rush.
dailyOverlaySettings.noModesYet: Your game modes will show up here after your first match — you can come back and change this anytime from My Account.

onboarding.welcomeText: Quick tour to show you where to find the main features — 30 seconds, you can skip anytime.
onboarding.searchText: Type here to jump straight to any tab, no need to dig through the menu.
onboarding.performanceText: Your gameplay stats: match history, recent form, death/kill heatmap, tactical analysis, teammates and rivals, charts, rank progress...
onboarding.myAccountText: Your Hall of Fame, things to work on, skin collection, tilt tracking, and network monitoring — everything specific to you.
onboarding.tournamentsText: Register for community tournaments and follow ongoing brackets.
onboarding.trainingText: 3D Aim Trainer (training modes, moving agents on the Monastery A site, Sensitivity Finder, weapons and skins) and guided warmup session.
onboarding.toolsText: Sessions, crosshair library, strategy board, team compositions, buy simulator, lineups, clips, team search, skin catalog, wiki.
onboarding.endText: You can replay this tour anytime from Settings, under “Security and account”.
